stem: A preoperative client has no formal diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but the STOP-BANG screening result places the client in a high-risk category. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: The screening result confirms OSA, so no further clinical evaluation is needed
options.B: The result identifies increased likelihood of OSA and perioperative respiratory risk; communicate it to the anesthesia/procedural team and incorporate it into risk planning and postoperative monitoring
options.C: The result is unrelated to anesthesia because STOP-BANG is used only after a sleep-study diagnosis has already been made
options.D: The result should be ignored unless the client develops apnea while awake in the preoperative area

rationale: STOP-BANG is a screening and risk-stratification tool, not a diagnostic sleep study. A high-risk result suggests increased probability of clinically important OSA and should be communicated during perioperative planning. OSA risk is relevant because affected or high-risk surgical clients can have greater respiratory and other postoperative complications, particularly when sedatives, anesthetics, and opioids are involved. The screen should therefore inform assessment and monitoring rather than be treated as definitive diagnosis or ignored until overt apnea occurs.
educational_objective: Interpret a high-risk STOP-BANG result as a perioperative risk signal—not a definitive OSA diagnosis—and communicate it so anesthesia and postoperative respiratory monitoring can be individualized.
source_organization: NCBI Bookshelf / StatPearls; BMC Anesthesiology via PubMed/PMC
source_document_title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea; Obstructive sleep apnea screening and risk of postoperative complications in adult surgical patients
source_version_date: StatPearls last updated 2025-03-04; BMC Anesthesiology published 2026-05-13
source_locator: Obstructive Sleep Apnea — History and Physical/Evaluation: STOP-BANG is a widely accepted screening tool for OSA probability. BMC Anesthesiology 2026 — Conclusions: high-risk OSA by STOP-Bang is independently associated with increased postoperative complications and supports perioperative risk stratification/management.
source_claim_supported: STOP-BANG screens for OSA probability rather than establishing diagnosis; high-risk screening status is clinically relevant to perioperative complication risk and postoperative planning.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — provide preoperative care; identify risk factors associated with procedures/anesthesia; recognize potential complications and communicate significant findings
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative OSA risk screening and monitoring planning
correction_summary: Replaced tool-purpose recall with clinically meaningful interpretation of a high-risk screen. Explicitly separated screening from diagnosis and linked the finding to perioperative communication and monitoring without imposing a universal monitoring protocol or numeric STOP-BANG cutoff.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current StatPearls 2026 edition and 2026 perioperative STOP-Bang outcomes study reviewed.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Screening-not-diagnosis role, OSA probability, and increased perioperative complication association are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; STOP-BANG does not by itself diagnose OSA.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; uses the screen as a risk signal for perioperative planning.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; STOP-BANG is specifically used to identify undiagnosed/high-risk OSA.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; perioperative risk exists without awake apnea in preop.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B correctly distinguishes screening from diagnosis and converts the result into safe perioperative action.
audit_findings.cueing: All options interpret the same high-risk result.
audit_findings.blueprint: Existing Reduction of Risk Potential blueprint is appropriate and retained.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked whether high-risk STOP-BANG mandates a specific monitoring level or OSA diagnosis; final wording avoids both unsupported claims.
